_note: PROTOTYPE review notes for #142, written by the prototype agent after looking at every image (montages plus full-size crops). Edge counts come from a brightness check of 12 px edge strips, confirmed by eye.
summary: Canon text alone (B) fixes costume: Peter's oatmeal tunic and rust-orange mantle in 15/15 images, and Moses's red mantle, white beard and crooked staff in 9/9, in all three styles, at today's 5 credits and ~4 s. In A, Peter's clothes change every verse.

Reference images (C) add place identity: Galilee becomes one recognisable lake (the same flat-topped cliff, snowy Hermon, black basalt shore, tarred boats) in all 18 C images. No reference was pasted in as a backdrop, but the cliff lands on the right in about 14 of 18, a framing bias. Faces get somewhat closer to the sheet; the grey beard streak shows in close shots, while the scar and crooked nose are too small to read at 1K.

The section look holds Exodus 14 together in B and C: red-brown mountains, blue-green water walls, the amber pillar glow and night-to-dawn light recur across 14:21, 14:22 and 14:27. A has no shared palette or landscape.

On Lite, Classical reference sheets pull Stained Glass back toward painting (Luke 5:8 C-Lite reads as Classical). 3.1 Flash keeps all three styles with the same references; Lite needs a per-style sheet (D1) or a style reference (D2).
3.1 Flash is at the latency ceiling: p50 9.6 s, p90 10.6 s, max 10.9 s, 9 credits. Lite with up to 3 references stays at 5 credits, p50 5.0 s, p90 6.6 s.

With at most 3 references there were no duplicated Peters or Moses and no text artifacts. Two problems remain: a canon character is added when the plan omits him (Moses in 14:22: 9 of 9 B and C images), and other apostles pick up Peter's rust colour in Acts 2:14.

Style negatives still leak in every condition. About a quarter of Watercolor images keep white paper margins. Stained Glass keeps black frames, arched tops or window side panels, including all 5 D1 images, whose per-style sheet has a lead frame.

conditions.peter--A-lite: Peter's clothes change every verse: grey, green, brown, blue. His face, beard and hair are generic. Galilee's shoreline differs each time. Jesus is drawn in the conventional European way in several cells.
conditions.peter--B-lite: Same rust mantle and oatmeal tunic in 15/15, with curly black hair and the grey chin streak in close shots. The scar and crooked nose are not visible at 1K. Galilee varies: text alone brings cliffs and a snowy peak, but not one geography. In Acts 2:14 other apostles pick up rust tones.
conditions.peter--C-lite: Costume as in B; the face is closer to the sheet (receding curls, broad face, grey streak). Galilee reads as one place, with no pasted backdrop, but the cliff sits on the right in most cells. Stained Glass weakens: Luke 5:8 reads as Classical, Matthew 26:75 has window side panels and Acts 2:14 has arched corners. White margins in 3 of 5 Watercolor cells.
conditions.peter--C-flash: Identity as in C-Lite with crisper faces, and all three styles render clearly, including Stained Glass. Galilee is the same place in 9/9, with the cliff on the right in 8/9. 9 credits, p50 9.6 s.
conditions.peter--D1-lite: Strongest Stained Glass rendering on Lite, but every Stained Glass cell has a black frame or an arched top (the sheet's lead frame leaks), and the mantle drifts to crimson as on the sheet. The Watercolor sheet adds little over C.
conditions.peter--D2-lite: The style reference recovers most of the Stained Glass look while Peter keeps his true rust colour. Window side panels remain in Matthew 26:75 and Acts 2:14. Three references caused no duplicate figures; Acts 2:14 shows mild costume bleed.
conditions.exodus--A-lite: Moses's robe and staff change per verse, and the three verses share no landscape, light or palette. Stained Glass has black frames and window mullions.
conditions.exodus--B-lite: Moses fixed in all 9. The section look's red-brown mountains and amber pillar glow recur, and the night-to-dawn progression is followed. Moses is added to 14:22, whose plan shows only the people crossing.
conditions.exodus--C-lite: Like B: the Red Sea reference adds no visible location gain over the text, and none of the images copied its calm-sea view. Moses is added to 14:22. One Stained Glass cell has an odd gold rectangular 'pillar'.
conditions.exodus--C-flash: Moses and the section palette are the most uniform of any condition, but Watercolor 14:21 is drawn in daylight against the section look's night. Moses is added to 14:22. 9 credits, p50 9.6 s.

cells.exo-14-21--watercolour--C-flash: Daylight, look says night; white margins
